builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions
summary: MPQ replaces the jointly learned latent codebook inside a skill policy with an external library of demonstrated motion prototypes, snapping each predicted action chunk to its nearest library element and correcting it toward the prediction within a bound, with no trained parameters. It costs a nearest-neighbor lookup and stored demonstration library at execution time, adds no training overhead, and the paper reports no measurable closed-loop performance loss across six architectures including a 7B VLA model. It can fail to transfer if the library does not cover the deployment distribution, and its offline reconstruction metrics are shown to misjudge library size, design, and cross-benchmark transfer, so validation must be closed-loop.
rationale: MPQ is a parameter-free, low-compute diagnostic wrapper, but it only applies to discrete-skill robot and vision-language-action policies, so it is worth adopting only if the reader's production work involves such systems.

claims.statement: MPQ replaces the jointly learned latent codebook inside a skill policy with an external library of demonstrated motion prototypes, snapping each predicted action chunk to its nearest library element and correcting it toward the prediction within a bound, with no trained parameters. It costs a nearest-neighbor lookup and stored demonstration library at execution time, adds no training overhead, and the paper reports no measurable closed-loop performance loss across six architectures including a 7B VLA model. It can fail to transfer if the library does not cover the deployment distribution, and its offline reconstruction metrics are shown to misjudge library size, design, and cross-benchmark transfer, so validation must be closed-loop.

Wrapped policies are statistically equivalent to the originals across six architectures; on LIBERO-90, quantization costs nothing, skill choice costs at most 2 success points, and the selectors' own placement and correction account for up to 12 points of the remaining gap.
